# How to sharpen a kitchen knife

You need a whetstone with a coarse side (around 1000 grit) and a fine side (around 6000 grit), a towel, and ten minutes. Soak the stone in water until it stops releasing bubbles, usually five to ten minutes.

- Place the stone on the towel so it cannot slide.

- Hold the knife at about fifteen degrees to the stone. A stack of two coins under the spine gives roughly the right angle.

- Push the blade across the coarse side, heel to tip, ten strokes per side. Keep the angle steady; the angle matters more than the pressure.

- Repeat on the fine side with lighter strokes.

- Wipe the blade and test it on a sheet of paper. A sharp edge slices cleanly without tearing.

Most home cooks need to do this every month or two. Honing with a steel between sessions keeps the edge aligned but does not replace sharpening.
